title: College Cost Truce Room
oneLiner: A family decision room that turns dream-school tension into a calm budget, loan, scholarship, and transfer-path negotiation before applications harden.
targetUser: Middle-income parents and college-bound students who need a shared plan before admissions, aid letters, and Parent PLUS loans become emotional fights.
keyUX: Parent and student enter budget limits, dream schools, in-state options, scholarship targets, transfer paths, and debt boundaries; the app turns them into a negotiated school list and conversation script.
requiredUISections: Net price and loan scenario board

externalSignalRefs.source: Reddit r/ApplyingToCollege, "Parents, the college loan convo feels backwards to me"
externalSignalRefs.observed: Parents argue the money conversation needs to start early, before dream-school attachment and Parent PLUS debt create panic.

externalSignalRefs.source: Reddit r/ApplyingToCollege, "Parents (or students) - anyone sad or disappointed? Middle class woes"
externalSignalRefs.observed: Families just above aid thresholds feel punished, unable to afford preferred schools while seeing others receive aid.

stitchPrompt: Design a responsive family finance product called College Cost Truce Room for middle-income parents and college-bound students who need a shared plan before admissions, aid letters, and Parent PLUS loans become emotional fights. Users enter household budget limits, dream schools, in-state options, scholarship targets, transfer paths, parent debt boundaries, student contribution options, and non-negotiables; the app converts the tension into net-price scenarios, emotional tradeoff cards, a practical school-list mix, and a conversation script both sides can accept. Include a family budget boundary intake, dream-school attachment map, net price and loan scenario board, scholarship and transfer-path planner, parent/student concern cards, tradeoff voting lane, college-without-going-broke script, and shareable family agreement memo. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with reassuring spacing, warm but not beige-heavy surfaces, plain-language finance cards, gentle tension meters, and clear next-step controls so the experience feels like a family truce room instead of a debt calculator.
